course_name_original: Elasticidad y Resistencia de Materiales I
course_name_en: Elasticity and Strength of Materials I
prerequisites: Having taken the courses Physics I, Physics II, Algebra and Geometry.

The student must master the following subjects: calculation of centroids, moments of inertia, static moment, matrix and vector operations, graphical representation of functions, equilibrium conditions.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Knowledge and use of the principles of strength of materials.
Competence in applying ethical principles related to sustainability values in personal and professional behavior.
Competence in the sustainable use of resources and in preventing negative impacts on the natural and social environment.
To know and use the principles of strength of materials.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1.- Introduction to strength of materials. - Stress state of a mechanical prism. - Prismatic bars and bar structures according to working mode. - Types of external actions. - Types of supports, degrees of freedom and reactions. - Isostatic and hyperstatic structures. - Stresses or forces in cross-sections. - Diagrams of: axial force, shear force, bending moment. - Relationship between bending moment and shear force. - Safety coefficient.

Topic 2.- Tensile and compressive stresses. - How to solve an elastic problem for elements subjected to both pure tension and compression. - Calculation of articulated structures / trusses. - Introduction to the concept of buckling for articulated elements subjected to compression.

Topic 4: General theory of bending. Stress analysis. Pure bending: - Pure bending in prismatic bars. - Navier's law. - Section modulus. Simple bending: - Generalized Navier-Bernoulli hypotheses. - Colignon's formula. - Principal stresses in simple bending. Compound bending.

Topic 5. General theory of bending. Deformation analysis. - Elastic curve, deflection and slope. - Methods for determining the deformation of a beam subjected to bending. - Stress/strain relationship diagram. This section will be expanded in ERM II.

Topic 6.- Lateral bending: Buckling. - Euler's critical load. Limits of application of Euler's formula. - Buckling length. - Concept of slenderness. - Eccentric compression. - Design of bars subjected to buckling.
Topic 7. Torsion. - Torsional moment diagram. - Stresses and deformations in solid circular and thick-walled hollow circular sections.
teaching_methods: Theory classes: Theoretical/practical classes. Possible teaching-learning methods: - Expository method/master lecture - Flipped classroom methodology. - Case study. The professor explains the competencies and objectives to be achieved. Basic contents of a topic are taught in a structured way. Typical exercises and particular cases are presented to reinforce the contents.

Practical classes, seminars, and problem-solving: Practical classes. Teaching-learning methods: Exercise resolution. Problem-based learning. Application activities are developed for specific exercises, with didactic content that allows deepening and expanding theoretical knowledge, with special emphasis on self-learning. Students develop appropriate solutions, follow procedures, and interpret results. Self-assessment exercises are carried out for each topic.

Workshop/laboratory practices: Laboratory Practices. Teaching-learning methods: Performing tests related to the theory explained in the course. Experiment-based learning. Tests are developed that allow students to experimentally verify theoretical knowledge and interpret the results.
assessment_rules: Progress tests account for 20% of the grade. The laboratory practice report accounts for 5%. The final exam accounts for 75%. Mandatory attendance for all laboratory practices and submission of the corresponding report. The use of IAG tools for report preparation is not permitted, nor is the use of electronic devices in exams.
